paper.title_en: HADAR's observational prospects for cosmic-ray anisotropy
paper.abstract_en: The characteristic structure of cosmic-ray anisotropy around 200 GeV provides a key opportunity to study the origin and propagation of cosmic rays. With an anisotropy amplitude of only $10^{-4}$ at this energy, this regime is particularly well suited for testing anisotropy models. Existing space- and ground-based experiments have not yet achieved sufficiently accurate measurements of this structure. The High Altitude Detection of Astronomical Radiation (HADAR) experiment may be particularly well suited to address this issue. This paper presents the expected HADAR observations of large-scale cosmic-ray anisotropy in the 0.1-10 TeV range. The analysis indicates that HADAR should achieve the statistical precision required to resolve anisotropy amplitudes of approximately 0.01% and to constrain the dipole phase with good angular resolution. In addition, the expected two-dimensional skymaps were simulated, clearly displaying the anisotropy structures. These results suggest that HADAR will substantially improve observational tests of the origin and propagation of cosmic rays.
